I've checked the project. kanbanr 0.6.0 is installed and this folder isn't tracked yet. You've already picked TOGAF with sprints and releases, so I only need a few more answers, one at a time.

**Where should the board live?** It's its own git repo and should sit outside the project folder.

1. `<run>/project.kanbanr`, a new folder beside the repo (recommended)
2. A different path you give me

The repository gives me very little to draft from. The README is a single line, there's no manifest, and there are no docs. So most of this charter has to come from you. Here is what I can fill in, with everything else left blank:

**Charter (draft)**

- **Purpose:** A scratch project used to walk through the TOGAF process with kanbanr. *(from the README; correct me if the real purpose differs)*
- **Vision:** *(blank)*
- **Goals:**
  - G-0: The system stays operable and maintainable. Measure: *(blank)*. This is a standing goal so chores link to something honest.
  - *(no others yet)*
- **Non-goals:** *(blank)*
- **Stakeholders:** *(blank)*
- **Constraints:**
  - Work follows the TOGAF process, in sprints and releases.
  - Nothing is pushed except by you.
  - Main must be pushed before anything is tagged. *(from your request)*

**Question 1: what is this project for?** Your answer settles the purpose, and the goals, non-goals and stakeholders follow from it.

1. Keep the draft purpose as it stands: a scratch project for exercising the TOGAF process (recommended if that's really all it is)
2. Tell me the real purpose, plus any goals and non-goals you have in mind

Two things are still open and I'll ask each in turn:
- **The board location.** My earlier question is unanswered. The recommended option is `<run>/project.kanbanr`.
- **Whether the project has CI.**

I'll set up the release stages after the board exists. Making main be pushed before the tag is a `kanbanr config release-stage` setting, so I need the board first.

Thanks. From this folder my check doesn't find that monitor. It looks at localhost:8080, and nothing answers there. That's expected, because no board exists yet for the monitor to read. I'll use your address, <monitor_url>, for every decision once the board is set up.

For the sprint I'll ask its goal and capacity, and I'll recommend starting it today. For the release I'll ask its version and target date.

I've noted the test, but I can't add it yet. There's still no board, so there's no basket item to attach it to. I've asked for the board location twice now, and nothing else can be created until you answer it.

Your test is open the basket page, add an item, close the browser, reopen the page, and the item is still there. When I define the item, I'll put it under the requirement that the basket is kept between visits. One thing I'll raise then: kanbanr reserves manual tests for a person's judgement, such as whether something reads well. A browser close-and-reopen check is something an automated run can see. I'll propose it as an automated walkthrough test, and you can still ask for it to be manual.

A reply of just "1" is enough. It puts the board at `<run>/project.kanbanr`, beside the repo and outside it.
